'''Ronald D. Macfarlane''' (born February 21, 1933, [[Buffalo, New York]])<ref name="OH"/> is distinguished professor of Chemistry at [[Texas A&M University]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.chem.tamu.edu/rgroup/macfarlane/ |title=Macfarlane Research Group |publisher=[[Texas A&M University]] |accessdate=November 13, 2010 }}</ref> In 1991, he received the Inaugural Award of the [[American Society for Mass Spectrometry]]'s Distinguished Achievement Award.<ref name="OH"/>

== Early life and education ==
* 1954 [[University at Buffalo]], New York - B.A. Chemistry<ref name="OH">{{cite web|author=Center for Oral History| title= Ronald D. Macfarlane |url=https://oh.sciencehistory.org/oral-histories/macfarlane-ronald-d |website= [[Science History Institute]] }}</ref>
* 1957 [[Carnegie-Mellon University]], Pennsylvania - M.S. Chemistry<ref name="OH"/>
* 1959 Carnegie-Mellon University, Pennsylvania - Ph.D. Chemistry<ref name="OH"/>

== Research interests ==
* Separations Methods for Medical Diagnosis
* Ultra-Sensitive Mass Spectrometry
* Is researching the new methods of [[Concept learning|Conceptual Learning]]

== Awards ==
* [[Guggenheim Fellowship]], 1968
* Distinguished Achievement in Research Award
* ACS Nuclear Chemistry Award
* 1990 ASMS Distinguished Contribution in Mass Spectrometry Award
